title: Fed Error? More Concern, Yields RISE MORE, Little Iran News, AI FEAR
speaker: Kevin Paffrath (Meet Kevin)

macro_themes.view: WSJ 'funding gap' warning signs aren't present; oversubscribed CoreWeave debt shows capital window still open, so it is too early to be mega-bearish.
Lisa Cook's piece suggests hiking into AI-driven sector inflation would be a mistake; outside geopolitics most forces ahead are deflationary.
Expects an Iran deal soon ('shilling this Iran deal hard'); a deal could take oil from ~$105 to $70-80 and make 'no more hikes this year' ~30% likely vs 10% priced.
10-year ~5.23% after 5.26%; TLT keeps sliding toward a long-term support line.
Agentic AI needs little CPU compute; frontier GPU spend (Nvidia/AMD) is where the money is, and Anthropic/OpenAI funding plus the labor market are the canaries.

calls.condition: Short term hinges on Iran: a deal lifts everything, no deal and 'everything might go down'.
calls.reason: Bubble 'ain't over yet' because capital is still flowing to AI (no funding gap); dips are buyable while the window is open.
calls.quote: my opinion is you should buy it because the bubble ain't over yet

calls.condition: If an Iran deal comes within ~5-6 weeks, oil drops from ~$105 to $80 or $70.
calls.reason: Expects a US-Iran deal (sanctions relief for nuclear steps); says he sold puts on something that benefits from a deal.
calls.quote: if we get an Iran deal ... oil goes from $105 to $80 or $70 ... I think it's going to happen

calls.reason: Frontier-chip spending by AI labs and Elon is where the money is; Nvidia does ~$100B/quarter in data center vs a rounding-error CPU agent market.
calls.quote: throw it in Nvidia and AMD for Frontier chips. That is a good trade

calls.reason: CPU/agent enthusiasm overblown: AMD ran from mid-$400s to $645, overbought daily and weekly; agents need few CPUs. Still calls AMD a great company and frontier chips a good trade.
calls.quote: in the short term, who knows? But longer term, we're probably a little overblown on CPUs

notes: Date: the CNBC closing bell clip says 'this Monday' (Sep 28); listing approx_date is 2026-09-29. Kevin says Micron reports 'tomorrow', while Ricky Gutierrez (Tuesday Sep 29) also says Micron is 'tomorrow', so one is a day off. AMD call is mixed (bearish on the CPU narrative, positive on frontier chips); quoted 645 is the recent high, not close. Skipped: CRWV (balance-sheet criticism, 'probably okay for now', no price view), MSFT (cash vs bills concern, he holds it), INTC, MU (earnings tomorrow, no bias), AXP, GME, TLT (only notes it falling toward support; considered but didn't buy calls).
